target_customer: Mexican homebuyers who need a mortgage and are underserved by banks
problem: Getting a mortgage in Mexico was slow, opaque and often denied. Kredi digitized origination and comparison so buyers could find and close a loan faster.
business_model: Mortgage broker fees at first, then own mortgage origination with interest income (from 2022 per a review)

founders.name: Javier Aldape
previous_startups: A previous startup he was exiting when denied a mortgage (name not given)
founders.background_notes: Crunchbase News says the idea came after he was repeatedly denied a mortgage in Mexico.

founders.name: Juan Carlos Mercado
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a Ruby and Elixir developer with 15 plus years of experience.

founders.name: Fernando Nader Giacoman
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and in Crunchbase News.

founders.name: Hernan Belden
founders.background_notes: Named as a co-founder in Crunchbase News, not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Creditas
competitors.what: Brazilian secured lending fintech that began operating in Mexico in early 2021 (home and auto equity loans)
competitors.funding_then: Large venture backing (amount not verified here)

competitors.name: Traditional Mexican banks and Infonavit
competitors.what: Incumbent mortgage lenders with branch based processes, compared in rankings of best mortgage credit

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly workflow software, bank integrations and credit scoring on top of Mexican credit bureau data. Origination later required a regulated lender license.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace and broker model was copyable. The later licensed lender entity (SOFOM) adds some regulatory position.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Kredi. As of the company site it is not currently offering new credits.

market_need_then: Mexico had a large mortgage gap and complaints about slow, denied applications. The founder cited his own repeated denial. The company reported over 8 million dollars of loans originated in early 2021 and 30 percent monthly revenue growth (Crunchbase News, June 2021).

branding.domain_note: Operates on kredi.mx, a country domain, not an exact .com

identity.logo: A trademark filing describes a logo of two stacked circles and semicircles beside the word KREDI
identity.visual_style: Plain functional site with regulator logos
identity.voice_and_tone: Short informal Spanish addressing the reader as tu

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself found. The name is a generic credit pun (credit-like word) shared with other firms, though the Rocket Mortgage analogy was memorable.

pivots.to: Originating its own home purchase mortgages
pivots.why: Stated in a third party review (kardmatch); reason not given

outcome_analysis: Kredi raised a 2 million dollar round and a 3.1 million dollar seed in 2021 while reporting fast early growth and moved from brokerage to own lending in 2022. The company site now says it is not offering new credits, so the current state is unclear. A March 2026 ecosystem profile says it has served over 700 thousand families, but no later round was verified.
notes: One aggregator lists a 4.5M round in April 2022 and total 7.5M to 7.84M; unverified, not recorded as a round. Two sources date the 2M round differently (one says March 2021 via LatAm List; a dated listing says September 2021 for the 3.1M). Competitor search found nothing from Mexican digital mortgage startups dated at the batch except Creditas; Yave, Holacasa and Morgana appear later or undated.
